kernel_variant: Tier S2 — 4-token tile on top of B2 image2d. 1 work-item = 4 outputs x 4 W positions = 16 outputs. Each weight image2d texel is reused across 4 tokens within one work-item.

harness.constraint: W must be divisible by 4 — decode (W=1) handled by the B2 non-tiled kernel

notes: Throughput plateau on Adreno 830 climbed from ~655 to ~790 GOps/s (22% of peak int8). Speedup vs B2 (1.15-1.19x) is modest — the headline win remains B2 image2d (decode 14.8x).

Work-group size tested: 64 and 128, no observed difference. Bottleneck is therefore NOT WG geometry. Next likely causes: register pressure (16 accumulators per WI) forcing spill, or dot() instruction issue rate.
- sub-group cooperative reduction (cl_khr_subgroups) to split slice_I across lanes
- Larger output tile (8 or 16 outputs per WI) — needs careful register budgeting
- fp16 / half-tile output to halve memory bandwidth on write

Compared to ML Drift target ~1000+ prefill_tok/s on a 7B LLaMA-class model: we are at ~125 prefill_tok/s (32 layers x ~14.6 ms FFN at seq=128 with tile_w4) — still ~8x off in compute alone, but each subsequent perf pass narrows this systematically.
